transcript.text: How is everybody doing? Primitive Nomad here and welcome back to another Dragon Wilds video. This is going to be a full
guide to magic in the rune crafting system. Magic in Dragon Wilds is more important than being used for just staff
and casting attacks. Runes and spells are used throughout the game for combat, gathering, movement, exploration,
farming, building, repairing equipment, fast travel system, and a lot of the skill spells you unlock as you progress.
So, even if you mainly play melee or range, you're still going to use magic and rune crafting throughout your play
through. This guide I'm going to go over how spells work, the spell wheel, runes, rune essence, anim events, rune
crafting, and how all of these systems work together. But, first we're going to go over spells and the spell book. The
spell book is where you can see the spells you've already unlocked as well as ones you're going to gain later down
the track of each skill. Each spell shows you what it does and the runes required to cast it. One important thing
to understand is that not every spell comes from leveling magic. Dragon Wilds has skill spells spread across the 12
different skills in the game. So, you can unlock useful magic through wood cutting, mining, farming, agility,
construction, and other parts of the title. This means magic becomes useful even if you never build your character
around magic combat. You might unlock a spell that helps you gather resources faster, move around Ashen Fall a lot
easier, maintain your farm, repair your equipment, or assist you in combat scenarios. I would check your skills
regularly because you may have already unlocked a new skill without even realizing it. Or you might be close to
unlocking a skill that's going to assist you in different aspects of the game. Now, once you do unlock spells, you can
choose which ones you actually want available through your spell wheel. You don't need every spell equipped at the
same time and as you progress, you'll eventually have more spells than you realistically need on one wheel.
Switching the abilities that actually help your build. Keeping the wheel organized makes magic much easier to use
because you're not searching through your spell book every time you need something. Now, Dragon Wilds does offer
multiple spell books and the The I set it up is I have one for combat, one for exploration, and then I also have one
that I use to maintain my farm as well as crafting back at my base. Utilizing the spell wheel correctly and organizing
the spells on your spell wheel will assist you when casting these spells out in the environment or when you're in
different combat scenarios. Now, the main aspect to magic in Dragon Wilds are runes. Runes are the resource that power
all your spells. Every spell has its own rune requirement, and you'll need the correct runes in your inventory before
you can cast it. There are several rune types you'll use throughout Dragon Wilds, including air, astral, earth,
fire, water, nature, and law runes. Different spells use different combinations of these. So, over time
you'll want to keep a supply of several rune types instead of only crafting one. The good thing is in Dragon Wilds, you
do have a separate inventory tab to keep your runes in, and it doesn't take up inventory space. Now, some of these
runes are heavily connected to combat, while others show up more often in utility and skill spells. Law runes are
especially useful and one of the most important runes in the title because they are tied to the teleportation and
lodestone system. And this is how you fast travel in Dragon Wilds. Now, the other main resource behind rune crafting
is rune essence. You'll find rune essence geysers throughout Ashran Falls as you explore. These will give you the
essence you'll eventually turn into runes. These geysers will respawn after a few in-game days. You can shoot the
rocks out of the air with an arrow, and then you just mine these rune essence rocks, and I highly recommend you
collecting as much as possible. Early in the game, you may not feel like you need
a huge amount of runes. That changes as you unlock more skill spells, start using lodestones regularly, and
potentially using magic more often in combat. When you find a rune essence geyser, mine what you can and bring the
essence back to your base. Building up a supply naturally early on while you're exploring saves you from having to go
back specifically looking for more later. The next major part of magic in Dragon Wilds is rune crafting and rune
altars. Once you pick up rune essence for the first time, you're going to unlock a new crafting station called the
rune altar. You can use the rune altar to turn rune essence into the different rune types you've unlocked. As your rune
crafting skill increases, you'll gain access to additional rune types and become more efficient at producing them.
Now, there are two main ways to create runes at the altar, attunement and auto crafting. Attunement is the active rune
crafting method and the best option if you want to get more runes and more experience. Process starts by choosing
how strong you want to attune the runes. You'll move around the room looking for different resonance frequencies, which
can be weak, moderate, or strong. Each one changes the difficulty and the amount of bonus runes you can
potentially receive. Weak attunement gives you a 33% bonus, a moderate attunement gives you a 66% bonus, and a
strong attunement gives you a 100% bonus. But, keep in mind the stronger the attunement, the harder the next part
of the process becomes. And at lower rune crafting levels, you also have less time to find and lock in the frequency
you want. As your rune crafting level increases, the attunement phase lasts longer, which makes finding the stronger
frequency much easier. Now, keep in mind if you don't find the frequency you want, you can simply back out and try
again. You're not going to lose any of the rune essence you used to activate that rune if you cancel during this
part. Now, once you have locked in your attunement, you will move into the infusion phase. This is where the rune
starts filling with magical energy and cracks begin appearing across it. Your job is to seal those cracks before they
start draining the bonus runes you earned during attunement. You're going to move around the room and repair each
crack as they appear, and if too many cracks stay open for too long, you're gradually going to lose some of the
bonus rune output that you would have received. Now, just like every other skill, at lower rune crafting levels,
this part can last longer and become harder to manage because more cracks can appear while you're working. As your
rune crafting increases, you'll unlock upgrades that shorten the infusion phase, making it much easier to keep
everything under control. If you do manage to repair every crack before any of them begin draining your bonus,
you'll get a perfect infusion. Now, this is what you eventually should aim for because a strong attunement combined
with a perfect infusion gives you the best rune output and the best rune crafting experience. But, in my opinion,
when you're starting out, don't worry about getting that perfect every single time. A weak and moderate attunement are
much easier ways to learn how this system works. Now, the other more simple method is auto crafting. This skips the
attunement and infusion process completely and creates the runes instantly for you. It's a lot easier and
faster, but there is a pretty big trade-off. By default, auto crafting gives you a one rune essence to five
runes ratio compared to the potential one to 10 ratio you can get through a successful high-level attunement. It
also only gives you 25% of the rune crafting XP you would normally earn through the active method. As you do
level rune crafting, you're going to unlock efficiency upgrades for individual rune types that eventually
improve auto crafting to the same one to 10 conversion rate. Those upgrades come a lot later on in the track. So, for
most of your progression, I would use attunement when you're actively trying to level rune crafting or maximize your
rune supply. Auto crafting is better when you just want some runes quickly and don't want to go through the full
process. Now, there is another way to obtain runes out in the world of Ashfall, and this is anima vents. As
you're out exploring Ashfall, you're going to find anima vents tied to specific rune types. These give you
another way to build your rune essence supply while you're already out exploring. Instead of constantly
returning to your base whenever you're low on a certain rune, you can top yourself up and take advantage of the
vents you find throughout the world. I would mark useful anima vents on your map, especially law rune vents. There is
one right next to the church on the left-hand side when you're just starting out in Dragon wilds because, like I said
earlier, law runes become extremely useful and you're going to use plenty of these when you start traveling around
Ashfall more often. But, finding a reliable source can save you a lot of time in the end. And keep in mind these
vents, just like the geysers, will respawn after a few in-game days, so you can constantly go back and farm them.
Now, you'll also find these vents while exploring vaults and other areas of Ashfall, so make a habit of using them
when you come across them instead of simply walking past them. You do need rune essence in order to siphon out the
runes from that vent, so keep that in mind you're going to have to have a little bit of rune essence on you to do
the conversion and the siphoning of the vent. Now, rune crafting becomes more useful the further you get into the
game. At first, you're mostly going to be unlocking new rune types that you can use for different spells, as well as
combat styles. But, higher levels improve how efficiently you can maintain your rune supply. Now, you don't need to
necessarily stop everything and grind rune crafting immediately. I would just keep it moving naturally with the rest
of your progression, as well as your other skills and combat styles. Gather rune essence when you see it, use animal
events while you're exploring, and regularly craft the runes you're actually using. That keeps you from
reaching a point later on in your play-through where you've unlocked a lot of useful skills, but don't have the
rune supply to actually use them. Now, gathering rune essence throughout Dragon Wolds is not that difficult, but I
highly recommend you focusing on farming as many geysers as you can. Once you get used to the attunement and infusion
system, I would focus on using that primarily, because you're going to get the most yield of runes, as well as XP
for rune crafting. Now, I want to go over magic in terms of combat. Magic is one of the main combat styles in Dragon
Wolds, alongside melee and ranged. And the different elemental types have their own strengths. Now, one of the biggest
things in Dragon Wolds, it's not like other games where you will build your character around a specific combat
style. You're going to want to progressively level up all three combat styles together, because you're going to
utilize them in different scenarios, as well as against different enemy types. Now, currently in Dragon Wolds, the
three elemental damage types you can use with your staffs are air, fire, and water. Air magic is built around control
and knockdown. It can help you manage enemies in fights and create some space instead of simply standing there trading
damage. Fire magic focuses more heavily on damage and burning. You can apply damage over time through burn effects
and use it aggressively against enemy where fire is effective. Water magic focuses more on slowing enemies and
giving you additional survivability. Building water effects on enemies can reduce their movement and later give you
ways to recover health during combat. So, a simple way to remember the three is that air is great for control, fire
focuses on damage and burning damage over time, and water allows you to slow enemies as well as give you
survivability. Just like the other combat styles, the best option can depend on what you're fighting, and keep
in mind if one type of magic doesn't seem effective against an enemy, try another element or another combat style.
Keep in mind, like I said, different enemies that you encounter throughout Ashen Fall are going to be weak or
resistant to different elemental types as well as damage types depending on your build and weapon setup. Now, if you
want to use magic as your main combat style, you also want to keep your magic equipment progressing with you. As you
reach new regions, you'll find stronger staves, which are staffs, magic-focused armor, and other equipment that support
that style, like different jewelry types. Now, your rune supply is your ammunition for magic. If you're heading
into a boss fight, vault, or dangerous region with barely any runes, you're going to run out of attacks very
quickly, as well as you're going to have the inability to cast the amount of spells that you want to. So, before you
leave your base, be sure to check your rune costs of the spells you're using and bring enough to actually support
your build, as well as your favorite skill spells. Now, we've talked about skill spells a lot, and skill spells are
probably one of the most important things for new players to understand, because they're useful regardless of
your combat style, and you're going to use them in all avenues of Dragon Wilds. Dragon Wilds uses magic as part of
almost every major system. You unlock abilities that can help you gather resources faster, repair your equipment,
move around the world, maintain your farm, control enemies, and make normal survival tasks much easier. For example,
some skill spells allow you to quickly gather large amounts of wood or ore, while farming has spells that can help
water and maintain your crops. Agility gives you movement abilities, and other skills continue adding their own useful
spells as you progress. There's also plenty of different skill spells tied to crafting and your crafting stations,
make your crafting more efficient and a lot faster. So, even if you're using melee or range for most of your combat,
you should still pay attention to your spellbook and skill spells. You'll be using magic constantly for every single
thing you do in the title. Now, the main things to remember is magic in Dragon Waolds connects to almost every part of
the game. You gather rune essence, use rune crafting and anima events to build your rune supply, unlock new spells by
leveling your different skills, and organize the abilities you need through your spell wheel. Those spells can then
be used for combat, gathering, farming, movement, exploration, and a lot of the survival mechanics you'll be doing
throughout Ashenfall. So, even if you have no interest in playing a dedicated magic build, don't ignore rune crafting
or skill spells. Keep your rune essence stocked, maintain a good supply of the runes you use, and check your spellbook
frequently as your skills increase. This is just a quick rundown on magic and rune crafting in Dragon Waolds. If you
guys have any more questions, let me know down in the comments below. And anyone in the community, if you have any
more tips, tricks, or any insight you would like to give to new players on the magic and rune crafting system, help
them down in the comments below. And keep in mind, RuneScape Dragon Waolds is officially coming to Steam, the Epic
Games Store, PlayStation 5, Xbox, and Nintendo Switch 2 on September 15th, and it is available to be wishlisted now
across all platforms. If you guys enjoyed this video, drop a like on it and subscribe for all things Dragon
Waolds. That's what we do here. We love to have you. And as always, guys, stay happy, stay hyped, and have a beautiful
day.
